title: Illustrator Level 1
subtitle: For newcomers to vector drawing. Leave able to build logos, icons and print-ready art.
summary: A two-day introduction to Adobe Illustrator: draw with the Pen tool, build a logo and an icon set, and export artwork a printer will accept.
description_html:
Illustrator is the tool you reach for when artwork has to stay sharp at any size: a logo that goes on a business card and on a hoarding, an icon set that has to read at 24 pixels, a map, a label, a diagram. This two-day course teaches the drawing, colour and type skills that sit underneath all of that, in the order a working designer needs them.

Day one begins with document setup, because most of the problems that reach a printer start with a badly set up file. You then spend a long session on the Pen tool. It is the part of Illustrator people avoid, and the part that decides whether artwork looks drawn or looks assembled. By the end of the first day you will have traced a supplied sketch into a finished icon and built a six-icon set that aligns on a shared grid.

Day two moves to colour, type and output. You will construct a wordmark, learn why global swatches let you recolour an entire design by editing one chip, place and trace images, and assemble a one-page A4 flyer with bleed and trim marks. The final session is the one clients care about: exporting SVG, PDF/X-4 and PNG, knowing which to send where, and packaging a job so the printer receives the fonts and links along with the artwork.

The syllabus maps to the published exam objectives for the Adobe Certified Professional in Adobe Illustrator, which is delivered through Certiport. We prepare you for that exam. We do not award the certification, and no course can guarantee a pass. If certification is your reason for attending, say so on day one and your instructor will flag which sessions sit directly on the exam objectives.

You work on the same practice brief throughout, so the icon set, the wordmark and the flyer belong to one fictional client rather than to three unrelated exercises. You keep every file you produce.
certification_alignment: Prepares for the Adobe Certified Professional in Adobe Illustrator exam
outcomes: Set up a document with the right artboards, colour mode, bleed and units for print and for screen
Draw accurate paths with the Pen tool by tracing a supplied sketch through to a finished icon
Build a six-icon set on a shared 24 px grid so the icons hold together at small size and at poster size
Construct a wordmark using Shape Builder and Pathfinder, then keep both an outlined and an editable master
Apply global swatches and colour groups so that recolouring a whole design is a single edit
Set point type, area type and type on a path, and control it with character and paragraph styles
Place, link and embed images, and trace a hand-drawn logo with Image Trace before cleaning up its anchor points
Assemble a one-page A4 flyer with correct bleed, margins and trim marks
Export the same artwork as SVG, PDF/X-4 and PNG, and explain which file goes to which recipient
Package a job for a printer with the fonts and linked images collected alongside the artwork
prerequisites: No prior experience with Adobe Illustrator is needed.
You should be comfortable with your own computer: saving files, finding folders and installing an application.
Some Photoshop experience is useful but the class does not assume it.
audiences: Designers moving from Photoshop or Canva into proper vector work
Marketing and communications staff who produce artwork in-house
Print and prepress operators who receive Illustrator files and have to fix them
Students and career changers building a first design portfolio
Small business owners who want to control their own brand artwork

curriculum.title: Day 1, Morning — Documents, shapes and the Illustrator way of working
curriculum.summary: Set files up correctly, then build accurate artwork out of primitive shapes.

topics.title: Vector against raster, and when Illustrator is the wrong tool for the job
New document setup: artboards, units, bleed, RGB and CMYK
Panels, workspaces and the tools you will actually use
Drawing with primitives: rectangles, ellipses, polygons and live corners
Selection, grouping, isolation mode and the Layers panel

curriculum.title: Day 1, Afternoon — The Pen tool and the icon set
curriculum.summary: Learn the Pen tool properly, then draw a six-icon set on a shared grid.

topics.title: Anchor points, handles and the four moves the Pen tool actually makes
Tracing a supplied sketch through to a finished icon
Shape Builder and Pathfinder for fast, clean construction
Building a six-icon set on a 24 px grid with pixel-accurate alignment

curriculum.title: Day 2, Morning — Colour, type and the wordmark
curriculum.summary: Work with global colour and type, and construct a wordmark you could hand over.

topics.title: Fills, strokes, gradients and the Appearance panel
Global swatches and colour groups: recolouring a design from one chip
Point type, area type, type on a path, character and paragraph styles
Constructing a wordmark, outlining it and keeping an editable master

curriculum.title: Day 2, Afternoon — Images, layout and handing work over
curriculum.summary: Bring images in, build a flyer, and produce files other people can use.

topics.title: Placing, linking and embedding images, and Image Trace on a hand-drawn logo
Clipping masks, opacity masks and simple effects
Assembling a one-page A4 flyer with bleed, margins and trim marks
Exporting SVG, PDF/X-4 and PNG, and choosing between them
Packaging a job for a printer: fonts, links and a handover checklist

faqs.question: Do I need my own laptop?
faqs.answer: For live online classes, yes. You work on your own machine with Illustrator already installed, and you keep every file you make. For classroom sessions in Colombo a workstation with Illustrator is provided, although you are welcome to bring your own laptop if you would rather work on the setup you use at your desk. We send system requirements and a setup check about a week before the class.

faqs.question: Is the Adobe software included in the price?
faqs.answer: No. Illustrator is a subscription from Adobe and we do not resell licences. If you do not have one, Adobe offers a free trial that is long enough to cover the two days, and your employer may already hold licences you can be added to. Classroom seats in Colombo come with the software installed on the machine.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss a day?
faqs.answer: Every live session is recorded and the recording stays available to you for 12 months, so you can catch up in your own time. If you would rather sit the session again live, you can join the same half day in a later cohort at no cost, subject to seats being available.

faqs.question: Do you issue a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes. You receive a MyLearnPlus certificate of completion, issued by Livezen Technologies, naming the course, the version of Illustrator taught and the hours completed. That is a record of training, not an Adobe qualification. The Adobe Certified Professional certification is a separate exam sat through Certiport.

faqs.question: Does this course prepare me for the Adobe Certified Professional exam?
faqs.answer: It covers a large part of the published objectives for the Adobe Certified Professional in Adobe Illustrator exam, and your instructor will point out which sessions map to them. The exam itself is booked and sat through a Certiport testing centre and is not included in the course fee. We cannot guarantee a pass. If you go on to complete a second related professional certification, Adobe awards a Specialty Credential such as Visual Design.

faqs.question: Is there a free retake?
faqs.answer: Yes. You may repeat the same class once within 12 months at no charge, in whichever delivery mode suits you at the time, subject to available seats. People usually use it six to eight weeks later, once they have hit real work and know which parts they want to sit through again.

faqs.question: Can my employer be invoiced, and can we pay in rupees?
faqs.answer: Yes. You may repeat the same live class once at no charge, in whichever delivery mode suits you at the time and subject to seats being available; the terms are shown on the booking page. People usually take it up six to eight weeks later, once they have hit real work and know which sessions they want to sit through again.
